author: high
claim: If a finite bipartite graph G=(X sqcup Y,E) has a matching saturating X, then |N(S)| >= |S| for every S subseteq X.
evidence: Let M be such a matching and fix S subseteq X. For each x in S, let m(x) be the Y-endpoint of the unique edge of M incident with x. Every m(x) lies in N(S), and m is injective because distinct edges of a matching have disjoint endpoints. Hence S injects into N(S), so |N(S)| >= |S|.

links.statement: If G has a matching saturating X, then the Hall inequalities hold.

glossary.N(S): the set of vertices in Y adjacent to at least one vertex of S
glossary.m(x): the Y-endpoint matched to x by M
